topic: Sign in with Google (server-side OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect authorization-code flow) on Cloudflare Workers, first-party auth, no third-party IdP

scopes.notes: scope MUST begin with 'openid'; add 'email' to get email + email_verified claims; add 'profile' to (possibly) get name/family_name/given_name/picture/locale

pinning_advice.runtime_critical: Pin hono and jose exactly (no caret) for reproducible Workers builds; they are the correctness-critical deps for auth.
pinning_advice.tooling: wrangler/@cloudflare/workers-types/typescript can use caret ranges but keep workers-types in lockstep with the installed wrangler; regenerate Env types after updating wrangler.

flow_steps: 1. GET /auth/google (on your Worker): generate a cryptographically random `state` (>=32 bytes, e.g. crypto.getRandomValues -> base64url) and a `nonce`; set both in a short-lived signed httpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax cookie (e.g. oauth_state), then 302 redirect to the authorization_endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope='openid email profile', state, nonce, and optionally prompt=select_account / access_type.
2. Google authenticates the user and shows the consent screen; returns a 302 back to your registered redirect_uri with ?code=...&state=... (or ?error=...).

3. In GET /auth/google/callback: if ?error present, handle (access_denied, redirect_uri_mismatch, etc.). Read state cookie, delete it, and constant-time compare against the returned `state`; reject 400 on mismatch (CSRF guard).

4. Exchange the code server-side: POST to https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded body { code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, grant_type=authorization_code }. Use client_secret_post (or Basic). This must run on the server, never the browser.
5. Response JSON contains access_token, expires_in, token_type=Bearer, scope, and id_token (JWT, RS256), plus refresh_token only if access_type=offline and only on first consent.

6. Verify the id_token: fetch Google JWKS from jwks_uri (cache via Cache API / HTTP cache headers), verify the RS256 signature, then assert claims: iss in {'https://accounts.google.com','accounts.google.com'}, aud == your client_id (azp if present), exp not passed (and nbf/iat sane), and nonce == the nonce you issued. Use `sub` as the immutable user id (never `email`).

7. Upsert the user in D1 keyed by sub; create a session (see session_recommendation); set the session cookie; 302 redirect to the app (strip code/state from the URL to avoid leaking the code via Referer/logs).
8. Optionally call userinfo_endpoint with the access_token for extra profile fields, but the id_token already carries openid/email/profile claims.

session_recommendation.summary: Stateless-signed JWT session token stored in an httpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Lax cookie, backed by a D1 sessions table for revocation and rotation. Own the auth; no third-party session store.

cookie.name: __Host-session (or sid)
cookie.flags: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=... ; (use __Host- prefix for the session cookie, requires Secure + Path=/ + no Domain)
cookie.why_lax: Lax is sent on the top-level cross-site GET redirect back from accounts.google.com, so the state cookie survives the OAuth round-trip. Strict would drop it on the callback. Do NOT use SameSite=None unless you also need cross-site XHR embedding (None requires Secure and a third-party-cookie policy).

session_recommendation.token: JWT signed with HS256 using env.SESSION_SECRET (Hono `sign`/`verify` from 'hono/jwt' is sufficient; `jose` SignJWT/jwtVerify is the alternative). Keep the payload small: sub, sid, iat, exp, maybe role. Do not put PII in the token.

session_table_d1.purpose: Server-side revocation, rotation, and auditability without re-issuing tokens on every request.
suggested_columns: id TEXT PRIMARY KEY (random sid, also the JWT `sid` claim)
session_table_d1.middleware_checks: On each request verify JWT signature+exp, then SELECT the sid from D1 and reject if missing/revoked/expired. This makes logout and global sign-out instant.

rotation_and_expiry.short_lived: Session token ~15 min–1 day, OR use a single session cookie with a sliding window (refresh last_seen_at/expires_at when older than a threshold, up to an absolute max of e.g. 30 days).
rotation_and_expiry.rotate_on: Rotate the sid (create a new D1 row + cookie) on successful login and on privilege change; optionally rotate periodically (e.g. every 24h) to limit fixation/theft windows.
rotation_and_expiry.logout: Delete the D1 row (set revoked_at) AND clear the cookie.
rotation_and_expiry.secret_hardening: SESSION_SECRET must be a high-entropy string (>=32 bytes). Set it via `wrangler secret put SESSION_SECRET` for prod and a `.dev.vars` entry for local dev.

session_recommendation.hono_middleware_pattern: Use a small custom middleware: read cookie via getCookie(c,'session') (hono/cookie), verify with verify(token, env.SESSION_SECRET) (hono/jwt), load+validate the session row in D1, then c.set('user', user) and await next(); return 401 otherwise. Hono's `jwt` middleware (hono/jwt middleware) enforces signature/exp/iss/aud but does NOT do the D1 revocation lookup, so a thin custom middleware around it is recommended. Signed-cookie helpers (setSignedCookie/getSignedCookie) are async on Workers because they use WebCrypto.

csrf_recommendation.primary: OAuth `state` parameter (per-login, random, stored in a short-lived signed httpOnly SameSite=Lax cookie and constant-time compared on callback). This is the OAuth-spec-mandated CSRF defense and the most important one.
csrf_recommendation.state_changing_requests: Use Hono's built-in `csrf()` middleware (import { csrf } from 'hono/csrf') which validates Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site headers for unsafe methods with form content types; configure csrf({ origin: 'https://yourdomain' }) (and allow localhost for dev). This is the modern Fetch-Metadata approach and covers cookie-session form posts.
csrf_recommendation.defense_in_depth: Because the session cookie is SameSite=Lax, state-changing cross-site POSTs already omit it; adding Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site checks (csrf()) covers browsers/proxies that omit Origin. A classic double-submit token (random value in a non-httpOnly cookie + echoed in a header/field, compared server-side) is optional additional depth but not required if state + SameSite + csrf() are used.
csrf_recommendation.notes: Hono's csrf() only checks unsafe methods and form-sendable content types; pure JSON APIs with a SameSite cookie rely on CORS + Origin checks instead. Set secure response headers via Hono's secure-headers middleware (HSTS, XCTO, etc.).

gotchas: redirect_uri must match the registered URI EXACTLY: scheme, host, case, and trailing slash. A mismatch yields `redirect_uri_mismatch`.

Google redirect-URI validation rules: HTTPS required (http allowed ONLY for localhost/localhost-IP); hosts cannot be raw IP addresses (localhost IP exempt); TLD must be on the public suffix list; no userinfo subcomponent; no path traversal ('/..'); no open redirects; NO fragment component; no wildcards/non-printable/invalid-percent/%00 characters; query strings are discouraged.
Use `sub` as the unique user key, never `email` (email can change / is not unique). Verify `aud` == your client_id and `iss` in {https://accounts.google.com, accounts.google.com}.
Verify the `nonce` claim against the nonce you issued to prevent ID-token replay; `nonce` is recommended (and shown as Required in Google's OIDC parameter table).

Refresh tokens (and test-user authorizations) expire after 7 days while the OAuth consent screen publishing status is 'Testing'. EXCEPTION: if the app requests ONLY name/email/profile (i.e. `openid email profile` / userinfo scopes), there is no 7-day expiry and test users need not be pre-registered — this is the case for pure 'Sign in with Google'.

'Testing' publishing status allows up to 100 test users; an unverified app also triggers the 'unverified app' screen and a 100-new-user cap for sensitive/restricted scopes. `openid email profile` alone avoids the sensitive-scope warning.

Web-app (server) flow should NOT use the JS 'Sign in With Google' GSI library for token issuance when the requirement is server-side auth-code ownership; GSI is browser-only. Implement the code flow server-side instead.

The exchange POST must be server-side (client_secret never shipped to the browser). Google recommends choosing an OAuth library rather than hand-rolling, but for Workers there is no official Google Node client that runs cleanly on workerd, so use `fetch` + `jose` for verification.
On Workers there is no Node `crypto`/filesystem: use WebCrypto-based libs (`jose`, `hono/jwt`). `hono`'s signed cookies are async (WebCrypto HMAC-SHA256).

Secrets: never put SESSION_SECRET/client_secret in `[vars]`; use `wrangler secret put`/`--secrets-file` for prod and `.dev.vars` (gitignored) for local `wrangler dev`. `.env` is an alternative but do not use both `.dev.vars` and `.env`.

Local dev: run `wrangler dev` (defaults to http://localhost:8787). Register `http://localhost:8787/auth/google/callback` (and/or `http://localhost:8080/...`) as an authorized redirect URI. Cookie `Secure` flag will prevent the cookie from being set over plain http on localhost in some browsers — conditionally drop `Secure` when host is localhost during dev.
Cache the Google JWKS (createRemoteJWKSet handles caching/rotation) instead of calling jwks_uri per request; keys rotate infrequently and the endpoint is edge-cached.

Cloudflare D1 session lookups add a query per request; keep a small index on sid and consider short-lived JWTs + periodic validation if latency matters. Alternatively use KV/DO, but D1 is the stated choice.
Set `prompt=select_account` if you want the account chooser every time, and `prompt=consent` only when you truly need a fresh refresh token (it forces re-consent).
